problems.description: Destroys the entire seed application rather than building on it: index.ts collapses from a 200-line Express/JWT/SQLite auth API to a 4-line entry point (-199 lines), and the package identity pivots completely (name changed to 'ssg', auth dependencies dropped, new gray-matter/js-yaml/marked SSG deps added). The existing architecture, routes, and the seed's `export default app` surface are orphaned by the rewrite.
Measured convention score 0.55 with 66 naming violations (camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE flagged on index.ts and hello-world.ts), indicating inconsistent identifier casing in the committed code.

index.ts is now a bare launcher importing `run` from './src/cli' while package.json bin targets dist/index.js; the committed build setup must produce dist or the CLI entry is non-functional — entry-point/artifact chain should be verified.

strengths: Modular greenfield structure: a single CLI entry point delegating to src/cli, with 10 new files separating concerns into a src/ tree.
Test infrastructure was added up front (jest.config.js with ts-jest preset) rather than retrofitted.
The scaffold is internally coherent for an SSG product (package.json bin entry matched to gray-matter/js-yaml/marked dependencies).
commit_reviews.summary: A destructive rewrite that replaces the seed auth API with an SSG CLI — internally tidy, but it discards the existing architecture instead of fitting it, and carries the measured naming-convention violations (0.55).

problems.description: src/templates.ts is gutted to a one-line re-export shim (exporting the new module plus TemplateEngine) instead of being deleted and its single call site updated; a permanent compat layer that also widens the old module's public surface.

223-line engine + new runtime dependency (handlebars and 5 transitive deps promoted from dev) replace an ~80-line hand-rolled module; SonarQube delta confirms the cost at +6 smells and +24 cognitive complexity, with escapeHtml/pageMeta logic replicated in the new module.
Frontmatter index signature [key: string]: unknown loosens compile-time typing for the template/layout fields added to the Page type.
test/templates.test.ts covers the engine thoroughly, but ssg.test.ts was not extended to exercise the new build() -> TemplateEngine integration path.

strengths: Backward-compatible: renderPage/renderIndex/escapeHtml API preserved via re-export shim, so cli.ts and existing callers keep working with no breakage
Comprehensive test suite (231 lines) covering frontmatter-driven template selection, layouts, partials, triple-stache escaping, custom fields, error cases, and built-in fallbacks
Correct dependency hygiene: handlebars moved from devDependencies to runtime dependencies where it now belongs
Minimal, well-integrated change to build.ts/ssg.ts; new module is well-documented with exported constants and a clear layout/partials convention
Old hand-concatenated HTML templates fully removed rather than duplicated alongside the new engine
commit_reviews.summary: Clean, tested, backward-compatible introduction of a Handlebars template engine that replaces hand-rolled HTML string building (0 bugs, API preserved via shim), but note the measured convention score of 0.55 is a pre-existing artifact of untouched files (index.ts, hello-world.ts) — none of the 66 naming violations are in this commit's diff, whose own code follows TS conventions.

problems.description: SonarQube delta shows +38 cognitive complexity across just +3 functions (~12.7 per function on average) — the session-3 integration logic is substantially over-complex for its size.
Commit introduces +10 code smells with no compensating bug fix or refactor, and the static_site_gen story's integration session does not seem to have consolidated prior complexity.

Convention score is only 0.55 with 66 violations concentrated in index.ts and hello-world.ts (functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE) — code deviates from the TypeScript project's own naming conventions.
Modifying hello-world.ts during an 'integration' session suggests scaffolding/experimentation files are still being touched by production feature work rather than a clean integration surface.

Adds chokidar (file watching) and ws (websocket server) as production runtime dependencies — reasonable for an SSG dev-server live-reload feature, and package-lock correctly separates @types/ws into devDependencies.

strengths: Dependency declarations are correct: runtime deps vs dev types (@types/ws) are properly partitioned in package-lock.json, and transitive deps were correctly promoted out of dev scope.
No new bugs and zero duplication introduced (+0 bugs, +0.0% duplications).
Commit message and diff scope match the session intent ('integration') for the story pipeline.
commit_reviews.summary: The commit fits the SSG story's integration step and manages its dependency graph cleanly, but the high cognitive complexity (+38 over 3 functions), +10 smells, and poor convention score (0.55) make it a net regression in code quality.

problems.description: load-plugins.ts transpiles TypeScript at runtime via require('typescript') and drives Node's Module._compile/_nodeModulePaths internals from an ESM-style module — couples the build to CommonJS-specific machinery and Node internals, fragile to runtime changes.
PluginContext carries an undeclared dynamic property (context.helloWorld = 0) that must be narrowed with typeof checks and casts — erodes the type safety the rest of the typed codebase relies on.
Two parallel page-loading paths now exist — exported loadPages (MarkdownPlugin.render) vs build's loadRawPages + applyOnFile pipeline — creating behavior drift risk.
Plugin/config load failures degrade to console.warn and an empty plugin list, silently swallowing misconfiguration.
Measured cognitive complexity +35 for the refactor, concentrated in the plugin-module resolution/transpilation logic.

strengths: Coherent plugin hook lifecycle (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with per-plugin error isolation.
BuildResult output contract unchanged, so consumers of build() are unaffected by the refactor.
Existing TemplateEngine rendering surface preserved via TemplatePlugin (renderIndex/renderPage).
Markdown rendering cleanly extracted into MarkdownPlugin, unifying the prior inline markdownToHtml call.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent plugin-architecture refactor that improves extensibility but introduces moderate technical debt (runtime TS transpilation, type-unsafe plugin context, dual page-loading paths) and lands below baseline convention adherence (0.55, matching the measured score).

problems.description: Cache invalidation key omits plugin code: canSkip checks only source hash + templatesHash, so changes to plugins (e.g. markdown/template transforms) never invalidate the cache, yielding stale rendered pages served from a previous build.
cachedOutputFor() silently returns '' when a manifest entry is missing, writing blank HTML files instead of failing loudly — a corrupt/incompatible cache produces empty pages with no error.

Skipped pages bypass applyOnFile plugin hooks on subsequent runs; plugins that accumulate state across pages (e.g. global tag lists) will diverge between cached and freshly-rendered pages within the same context.pages.
Cognitive complexity +27 in build(): the render loop now mixes hashing, cache lookup, stats, and output bookkeeping; the skip/render decision and stale-output cleanup are good extraction candidates.

The mechanical convention score of 0.55 is contradicted by the violation list: all shown violations (camelCase/PascalCase/UPPER_CASE in index.ts and hello-world.ts) are in files untouched by this diff, not in the new cache.ts/build.ts code, which itself follows naming conventions.

strengths: Cache concerns are cleanly separated into a dedicated src/cache.ts module with typed interfaces (CacheManifest, CachedPage) and UPPER_CASE constant.

Composes with the existing plugin/template pipeline instead of bypassing it — cached pages still flow through context.pages and runSyncHooks, and applyOnFile/template.renderPage are reused for the hot path.
Extracts loadRawPageEntries/comparePages helpers, removing duplicated sort logic and keeping loadRawPages as a thin wrapper.
Adds observable value via BuildStats (pagesBuilt/pagesSkipped/timeSavedMs) and cleans up stale output files for deleted sources.
commit_reviews.summary: Net-positive incremental-build feature that fits the SSG's existing patterns, though it introduces technical debt via missing plugin-change invalidation, a silent empty-output fallback, and the 0.55 measured convention score appears driven by pre-existing violations in untouched files (index.ts/hello-world.ts) rather than this diff's code.

compounding_issues: Session 1's destructive rewrite of the mismatched auth-API seed (architectural_fit 0.2, 'worse') was necessary for the greenfield task, but naming violations in untouched files (index.ts, hello-world.ts) dragged the measured convention score to 0.55 in every later session.

Session 4's plugin system depends on runtime TypeScript transpilation (require('typescript') + module._compile) and a type-unsafe PluginContext, and left two parallel page-loading paths (loadPages vs loadRawPageEntries) in build.ts.
Session 5's incremental cache keys on content-file and templates-directory hashes but not on plugin definitions, so plugin changes silently fail to invalidate cached pages.

Session 3's dev-server accumulated high cognitive complexity (+38) and was never genuinely absorbed into the Session 4 plugin architecture (DevServerPlugin is a factory-only shim with no lifecycle hooks).
key_decisions: Greenfield rewrite of the seed into a modular SSG (src/build, src/ssg, src/cli, src/templates) with a jest test/ suite and a package.json bin entry.
Adopting Handlebars as the template engine with built-in fallback templates, layouts, and partials, cleanly replacing hand-rolled HTML string building (Session 2).
Lifecycle-hook plugin architecture (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) with runtime-loadable TS plugins from ssg.config.ts (Session 4).
Content-hash incremental build cache (.ssg-cache.json) with template-hash invalidation, stale-output cleanup, and time-saved statistics (Session 5).
Standalone dev server with chokidar watching, debounced rebuilds, WebSocket live-reload injection, and a directory-traversal guard (Session 3).
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the arc, with a mid-story dip. Session 1 produced a functional but architecturally disruptive greenfield core (1 test; reviewer: worse). Session 2 was the cleanest commit — a backward-compatible, debt-free template engine addition (reviewer: 0.8/0.8). Session 3 regressed on review due to high cognitive complexity in the dev server (longest session, 570s). Session 4 recovered with a net-positive plugin refactor despite runtime-transpile debt, and Session 5 landed a strong, pattern-fitting incremental-build feature (reviewer: better, 0.72). Tests grew monotonically (1→2→3→3→4 suites, 49 passing), and the final build scores correctness 1.0, constraint_score 1.0, and escape 0.861 — a mature, working SSG.
story_review.summary: A coherent five-phase SSG story — greenfield, template engine, dev server, plugin refactor, incremental caching — where the early destructive rewrite and Session 3 complexity were paid down by Sessions 4-5, ending in a correct, well-tested, extensible codebase.
